claims.text: Dynamic surface restructuring governs the catalytic activity of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic surface restructuring governs the selectivity of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic surface restructuring governs the durability of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy can elucidate dynamic changes in catalyst surface electronic and geometric structure.
The catalyst undergoes dynamic surface restructuring under ethanol-oxidation operating conditions.
Changes in electronic structure facilitate the electron and proton transfers involved in ethanol oxidation.
Changes in geometric structure facilitate the electron and proton transfers involved in ethanol oxidation.
The ethanol-oxidation process considered involves transfers of 12 electrons and 12 protons.
An optimized surface structure enhances catalytic activity.
An optimized surface structure enhances catalytic selectivity.
An optimized surface structure enhances catalyst durability.
The proposed relationship applies under operational ethanol-oxidation conditions.

contradictions.description: Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy is presented as a characterization method that elucidates restructuring, but the baseline is performance without characterization and the outcome implies enhancement. This conflates observing the catalyst with a controlled intervention expected to alter its performance.
